ruleName: Nonprofit donation page with a hosted-card-fields-style payment widget in a cross-document <iframe>. The embedded form re-implements its own tab cycle: the last control ('Donate $25') loops forward Tab back to the first field, and Shift+Tab from the first field loops to the last, so Tab cycles among the widget's controls forever and never crosses the iframe boundary to the parent's 'Cancel and return to home' link. No exit advice.

Forum thread reply box implemented as a custom element <comment-composer> whose UI lives in an open Shadow DOM (attachShadow mode:open, delegatesFocus:true). The light-DOM source is just the empty custom-element tag. The component listens for focusout on its shadow root and synchronously re-focuses the textarea, so Tab/Shift+Tab cycle textarea<->button forever and never cross the shadow boundary to the parent's 'Back to all threads' link. No Esc, no advice.

Transit service-update page embeds an interactive route diagram as a separate SVG document via <object type='image/svg+xml' data='case-05-map.svg'>. The SVG's four focusable station <a> links are looped by the SVG's own script (last->first on forward Tab, first->last on Shift+Tab) so Tab never crosses the object boundary to the parent's 'Next: fares & passes' link. A paragraph BEFORE the object reads 'Tab through the diagram, then press Tab once more to continue' — plausible G21-style advice that is in fact FALSE.

Long-form magazine newsletter gate built with the HTML popover attribute (popover="manual"). On load it pops open and grabs focus; a document focusin guard snaps focus back to the email field whenever it tries to leave (hand-built trap on top of the popover). It displays 'Not now? Press Esc to dismiss' but NO Esc listener is wired, and popover="manual" disables the UA's native light-dismiss/Esc-close, so the documented exit is false.

Cobalt Bank account-opening flow with ONE modal that is conformant containment in isolation: 'Verify your identity' opens a role=dialog aria-modal=true overlay, initial focus lands on a real focusable Close button, an Escape handler on the parent document closes it, Close/Cancel/Continue sit in the Tab cycle, and focus is restored to the opener. The defect is the embedded third-party format in the modal body: a 'SecureScan' KYC widget delivered as an <iframe srcdoc> second document whose own Tab-wrap and focusin re-grab keep focus circulating inside the frame forever, while the modal's Escape listener - living one document up - never receives keydowns fired inside the frame. A keyboard user can enter the verification step but cannot leave it.

Knowledge-base Markdown editor as a custom element <markdown-editor> in an open Shadow DOM. Inside the textarea Tab is deliberately captured to insert indentation (the WCAG rich-text-editor example), so plain Tab does not advance focus. BUT a persistent visible instruction inside the shadow root says 'Press Esc to leave the editor', and a working Esc handler blurs the textarea and moves focus across the shadow boundary to the host 'Publish' button. PASS boundary variant.

Podcast episode page embeds an audio-controls panel as a cross-document <iframe>. Inside are real focusable controls (Play/Pause, Rewind, Forward, seek slider, speed select). The player adds legitimate widget behavior (Play toggles label; range uses native arrows) but does NOT intercept Tab anywhere, so forward Tab on the last control falls through and crosses the iframe boundary to the parent's 'Show transcript' link. PASS boundary variant (G21 mechanism #1).

SaaS onboarding coachmark embedded as a cross-document <iframe src='case-01-frame.html'>. The embedded mini-app's only control, a 'Got it' button, swallows Tab (keydown preventDefault + self-refocus) and re-grabs focus onblur, so focus enters the iframe and can never cross back to the parent's 'Open dashboard' link. No Esc, no exit advice.

Government DMV vehicle-registration renewal modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). Focus IS restricted to the dialog (Tab wraps among its controls), but this is the legitimate-containment carve-out: a wired, functional Esc handler closes the dialog and restores focus to the triggering button, and the focus cycle explicitly includes the focusable header Close (✕) and footer Cancel. The conformant modal the ACT corpus never models.

SaaS analytics dashboard 'Create alert rule' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). It HAS a genuine focusable header Close button and footer Cancel button, but the hand-rolled focus trap was scoped to a hard-coded selector ('.dialog-form input/select/button') that matches only the form-body controls, so the wrap cycle excludes both dismiss controls. The user can see Close/Cancel but Tab can never land on them; no Esc handler either.

E-commerce (outdoor retail) product 'Quick view' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). A focus trap cycles Tab among the size/quantity/Add-to-cart controls. The only dismiss is a round '✕' that is a <span> with role=button + aria-label and an onclick handler only — not focusable (no tabindex, not a real button) and with no keydown; there is also no Esc handler. Closeable by mouse, trapped by keyboard.

Healthcare patient-portal refill modal built with native <dialog open>: a JS focus trap cycles Tab among the refill form's four controls, but there is no Close/Cancel control and no Esc handler. Because the dialog was rendered with the open attribute (not opened via showModal()) the UA's native Esc-cancel is not armed either; only a mouse backdrop-click escapes. Keyboard users are stranded.

Government public-library 'Renew library card' modal. Focus is contained (Tab cycles inside), there is NO advice text and the close control is labelled 'Cancel' not 'Esc', but pressing Esc dismisses the dialog and restores focus to the trigger. A naive checker sees a focus cycle with no documented exit and wrongly flags a trap; it actually passes because Esc is a standard exit method, so no advice is owed.

Restaurant online-ordering 'Browse menu' dropdown built as an APG role=menu with roving tabindex; arrows move among dishes but the keydown handler also preventDefault()s Tab/Shift+Tab and remaps them to item movement, so once focus enters the open menu it can never reach the promo field or the checkout button. No Esc, no documented exit.

Flight-booking departure-date picker built as an ARIA role=grid calendar (the canonical Understanding 'calendar widget' construct). Arrows navigate day cells, but the grid keydown handler captures BOTH Tab and Shift+Tab with preventDefault() 'to keep focus in the calendar until a date is picked', with no Esc and no instruction, so focus can never reach the Search flights button.

RTL Arabic real-estate filter page (دار السكن) with two visually and structurally identical ARIA listboxes. The left 'Area' listbox releases focus when arrowing past the ends (standard arrow-key exit, no advice owed = PASS foil); the right 'Property type' listbox clamps the arrows and only escapes via the undocumented non-standard combo Ctrl+Shift+X with no advice = FAIL. Page fails because of the trapping widget.

Job-application form with a roving-tabindex role=listbox ('How did you hear about this role?'). Arrows navigate options and Enter selects; the keydown handler deliberately omits any Tab case, so unmodified Tab carries focus OUT to the Submit button and Shift+Tab back to the Email field. The on-screen help wrongly says 'Use Tab to move between options' — a misleading mental model, but NOT a 2.1.2 failure because Tab still exits. Boundary PASS case.

SaaS analytics dashboard with a valid APG role=tablist (MRR/Churn/Cohorts/Forecast). Arrows move between tabs and Tab is NOT preventDefault'd, but each tab has a blur listener that refocuses the active tab on the next tick (setTimeout(()=>tab.focus())), so pressing Tab to leave the tablist toward the panel link or the Export button instantly snaps focus back to the tab.

RTL Arabic article-publishing editor with an APG role=toolbar (Bold/Italic/Underline/List/Link) using roving tabindex and aria-pressed toggles. In RTL, ArrowLeft advances; the handler also captures Tab and the movement WRAPS, so at the last button advancing loops back to the first instead of exiting — a closed within-widget loop with no exit index. The title field and Publish button are unreachable. No Esc, no instruction.

Online-banking step-up OTP verification modal (Meridian Credit Union). It DISPLAYS the advice 'Press Esc to cancel and return to your account', but the keydown handler compares e.keyCode === 13 (Enter; Esc is 27) by mistake, so the documented standard exit key never fires — advice and implementation disagree.

E-commerce headphones store with a custom div role=slider 'Max price' facet. Arrows (and PageUp/Down, Home/End) adjust the price with complete ARIA value semantics, but the thumb keydown handler also captures Tab with preventDefault() 'to prevent accidental value loss when you tab away mid-drag', with no Esc and no instruction, so focus is stranded on the thumb and cannot reach Apply, the brand checkboxes, or the product links.

Theatre box-office seat-picker modal (Aurora Hall). Both Esc and Close release focus, but the promo-code <input> calls stopPropagation() on its keydown, so Escape never reaches the dialog handler WHEN that field is focused. Esc works from the seat buttons and silently fails from the input — a positional trap that requires testing exit from EACH focus position.

Garden-centre 'New This Season' page: a 5-card featured carousel (Add-to-basket buttons) sits between header nav and footer nav. The last card's button has a keydown handler that preventDefaults forward Tab and focus()es the first card, walling off the footer links. No advice given.

Independent bookshop 'Staff Picks' page: structurally and visually the twin of case-01 — a 5-card carousel (Add-to-cart buttons) between header nav and footer nav — but the final card's Tab is deliberately NOT intercepted, so focus flows naturally from the last button to the footer's first link. No advice text because none is needed.

Knowledge-base note composer: a 6-button rich-text editor toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-labelled buttons) between a header nav and the editor/footer. A misapplied 'roving tabindex' binds Shift+Tab on the FIRST toolbar button to focus() the LAST button, so backward navigation can never reach the header nav. Forward Tab is fine; no advice.

Public-library account-signup form: a required email field suppresses a plain forward Tab while the value is not a valid e-mail (so it LOOKS like a trap), then releases focus to the password field, submit button and rest of the page the instant a valid address is typed by keyboard. Shift+Tab is never blocked. Conformant keyboard-satisfiable input gate (PASS boundary variant).

Healthcare clinic-finder: a 5-control 'Refine results' filters panel (Specialty/Distance/Insurance/Available selects+input and an Apply button) sits between a top results list and a bottom results list. Tab on the last filter ('Apply filters') is intercepted and focus returns to the first filter, so the bottom results section is keyboard-unreachable. No advice.

Car-insurance quote wizard, Step 1: a required postcode field intended as a gate uses a blur handler that re-focuses the field UNCONDITIONALLY (no validity check). After the user types a valid UK postcode (BS35 1HJ) by keyboard, every Tab/Shift+Tab/click-away snaps focus back to the field, so focus can never reach the date-of-birth field or Continue button. Genuine trap masquerading as a validation gate (FAIL).

Football live-match centre: a live-commentary sidebar widget (5 controls) intentionally loops Tab internally (plain Tab/Shift+Tab cycle within the panel), BUT a visible instruction reads 'Press Ctrl+M at any time to skip past the panel' and the Ctrl+M handler genuinely moves focus to the footer. The advice-clause contrast to the no-advice failing loops.

E-commerce checkout shipping step: the required street-address field is gated by an inline verification error and forward Tab is suppressed until the value exactly matches the carrier verifier's canonical string. The user's typed value is rejected, and the ONLY offered resolution is a mouse-only 'Use suggested address' button (<div class=fix onclick> with no tabindex/role/keydown). A keyboard user can edit the field but cannot reproduce the exact canonical string blind, and cannot activate the pointer-only Fix control, so they can satisfy nothing and forward Tab never advances (FAIL).

10K race-registration confirmation step: a required participant-waiver section suppresses forward Tab past the consent group until the user checks a native 'I accept the waiver' checkbox. It LOOKS like a trap to anyone who Tabs onward without checking, but the checkbox is a real focusable <input type=checkbox> toggled by Space; once checked the gate releases and Tab advances to Complete registration and the rest of the page. Shift+Tab is never blocked. Conformant required-interaction gate (PASS boundary variant).

SaaS workspace-onboarding wizard: Step 1 requires selecting a plan before advancing, but the plan selector is a pair of mouse-only plan tiles (<div class=tile onclick> with no tabindex/role/keydown). While no plan is chosen the Continue button stays disabled and focus is held inside Step 1 (blurring the workspace field bounces back). The required gating interaction has no keyboard path, so a keyboard user can never complete Step 1 or reach the rest of the wizard (FAIL).

Lease e-signature step: the signature region loops focus and exits on Ctrl+M, but the escape advice is locked in a popover opened ONLY by a mouse-only div[onclick] info badge (no tabindex/role/keydown). Even if opened, the tip says 'press Esc' — which is dead — so the advice is both keyboard-unreachable and inaccurate.

Webmail compose: a contenteditable rich-text editor captures Tab (WYSIWYG indent) and exits on Alt+0, but the only documentation of that keystroke is a title= tooltip on a non-focusable '?' badge — revealed on pointer hover only, never reachable or announced for the trapped keyboard user.

Rail-booking seat grid (arrow-key roving tabindex) traps focus; the visible, reachable legend says 'press Ctrl+M' to leave, but the keydown handler actually releases on Alt+M (right key letter, wrong modifier), so following the documented combo keeps the user trapped.

County property-tax estimator: a Millage Worksheet loops focus internally; the working custom exit (Ctrl+M) is documented ONLY inside a collapsed <details> placed in DOM/visual order AFTER the trap, so a trapped keyboard user can never reach or open it.

Patient-portal Care Plan Builder with two side-by-side focus-trapping panels: Morning (escapes Ctrl+J) and Evening (escapes Ctrl+K). Both panels display identical 'press Ctrl+K' help; correct for Evening but inaccurate for Morning, whose real escape is Ctrl+J.
